title: Rome takes justify morally as sanctify and cleanse
source_text: XLV. Jam vero Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, justificari sumunt non forensi, sed morali sensu. Estque justificari ipsis idem ac sanctificari, & a peccati sordibus mun-dari. Itaque quum pretendunt hominem formaliter justificari coram Deo per justitiam inhaerentem, id sibi volunt justitiam a Spiritu Sancto infusam, esse formam a qua fideles in Scriptura sancti justique nominantur, & per quam reapse tales constituuntur; non solum apud homines, sed etiam apud ipsum Deum, qui justitiam quam ipsis indidit probat & acceptat, ut veram & synceram: quae proinde in igne ultimi judicii, quum Christus vivos & mortuos judicabit, mansura & constitura est; & a Christo laudem & praemium vitae, & gloriae aeternae acceptura.
pass_a_gloss: But now the doctors of the Roman Church take being justified not in a forensic but in a moral sense. And for them to be justified is the same as to be sanctified and cleansed from the filth of sin. Therefore when they maintain that a man is formally justified before God by inherent righteousness, they mean that the righteousness infused by the Holy Spirit is the form from which believers in Scripture are named holy and just, and by which they are in reality constituted such—not only among men but also before God himself, who approves and accepts the righteousness he has implanted in them as true and sincere: which therefore in the fire of the last judgment, when Christ will judge the living and the dead, will remain and stand, and from Christ will receive praise and the reward of eternal life and glory.
pass_b_english: Rome takes justify morally as sanctify and cleanse from sin's filth.
Formal justification by inherent justice = Spirit-infused form naming and making them holy before God, lasting to final reward.

lemmas.gloss: not in a forensic but a moral sense
